blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Usual's official bUSD0 materials identify the token as a bond wrapper over USD0, while the USD0 technical documentation describes issuer or DAO-controlled minting and blacklist checks on the underlying token. A separate deployment-wide holder-freeze inventory for bUSD0 was not established, so the explicit Possible status is retained.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: bUSD0 has a reviewed Ethereum native bond-wrapper route and a distinct Ethereum-to-Arbitrum LayerZero V2 burn/mint representation route. The Ethereum L1OFTAdapter locks/releases canonical bUSD0, while the Arbitrum OFTMintAndBurnAdapter is the authenticated local token minter/burner. Adapter owners, endpoint peers, representation-token upgrades, and the LayerZero validation boundary are scored here; inherited USD0 routes are not substituted for bUSD0 evidence.

routes.protocol: Usual bUSD0 native bond wrapper / LayerZero V2 L1OFTAdapter
routes.reviewNote: Reviewed at Ethereum block 25771035 on 2026-08-16: Ethereum is the primary bUSD0 bond-leg deployment and its local issuance is the locked-USD0 wrapper path. The canonical-side LayerZero L1OFTAdapter at 0xd155d91009cbe9b0204b06ce1b62bf1d793d3111 is immutable, uses endpoint 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fe728c, and locks/releases canonical bUSD0; its peer for endpoint ID 30110 is the Arbitrum adapter. This route is native issuance, while the adapter's transfer-rail controls are separately authored below.

Reviewed at Arbitrum block 495301927 on 2026-08-16: the official deployment directory labels the local route OFTMintAndBurnAdapter 0xd155d91009cbe9b0204b06ce1b62bf1d793d3111. Its LayerZero endpoint is 0x1a44076050125825900e736c501f859c50fe728c, its peer for endpoint ID 30101 is the Ethereum adapter, and the route burns/mints the Arbitrum bUSD0 representation against the Ethereum lock/release side. eth_call mint(address,uint256) succeeded from the adapter and reverted from an unrelated EOA, so local token-level bridge mint authority is recorded as Bridge Risk. Current DVN/ULN configuration and numeric rate limits remain an evidence gap.

The adapter peer bound endpoint ID 30110 to the Arbitrum adapter. Safe module/guard state and current DVN/rate-limit values remain unverified.

controls.label: bUSD0 Arbitrum representation adapter mint/burn authority
controls.capDescription: The Arbitrum adapter is an authenticated token-level mint/burn caller. No independent token-level aggregate or per-call cap was evidenced; the documented route is supply-conserving only when Ethereum lock/release, Arbitrum burn/mint accounting, peer validation, and LayerZero validation remain correct.

routeChecks.trustedPeerOrRemote: The adapter's LayerZero peer is the Ethereum adapter for endpoint ID 30101; peer and endpoint administration is separately scored under the adapter-owner Safe.
routeChecks.onchainAmountBounds: At Arbitrum block 495301927, mint(address,uint256) returned successfully when called from the local adapter 0xd155d91009cbe9b0204b06ce1b62bf1d793d3111 and reverted from 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001. This proves authenticated representation mint authority; the route-level lock/release plus burn/mint conservation is not an independent native mint bound.
routeChecks.pausersAdminsUpgraders: The representation token accepts the reviewed adapter as its privileged mint caller. Representation-token upgrade administration is separately recorded under the Arbitrum ProxyAdmin owner Safe.

controls.evidence: At Arbitrum block 495301927, eth_call to the bUSD0 representation's mint(address,uint256) succeeded from the local OFTMintAndBurnAdapter 0xd155d91009cbe9b0204b06ce1b62bf1d793d3111 and reverted from unrelated EOA 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001. This local token-level bridge mint/burn capability is representation risk and is intentionally absent from Mint Authority.

controls.label: bUSD0 Arbitrum representation ProxyAdmin owner Safe
controls.capDescription: The Arbitrum bUSD0 ProxyAdmin can replace the representation-token implementation, so it can change the local bridge mint/burn authorization and any representation cap or pause constraints. This is not native Ethereum issuance authority.

routeChecks.caps: No independent representation-token cap or upgrade delay was evidenced in this pass; any cap or authentication constraint introduced by the current implementation remains upgrade-dependent.
